items.title: Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: Because if it was good enough for Joe Williams, it’s good enough for Javon Jackson.

ctx.x: Are there issues in the business of music, as far as getting gigs and so forth, that are non- musical, generational, racial, man/woman, anything like that. Does that come into play as far as you know?

Well, I look at it like this. You get on the phone, you make a phone call to a club, you mention to the club owner, “I’d like to work your venue.” And either they’re available or they’re not. Now available to you or they’re not. Now I know a lot of people, musicians that I know, will tell you well you can’t do it on your own and you can’t call clubs because they don’t want to talk to musicians, and I have found that to be the absolute nontruth. The festivals that we just played, I booked them, I have a rider, I…

and I’ve got this to offer, and who is this guy to tell me that he doesn’t like me and my value is this and that. That’s when you make it personal. But the business aspect of it is, guess what, this is what it is. Case in point: you called my house. You said, “Javon, I’d like to have you come and speak to me about your life and your career.” And we spoke about the price. I said, “Oh man, I don’t know if I want to do that” and I hung up the phone. And when I hung up the phone I thought about and I said you know…
